summary: Eastern Lane FPA lookout on Table Mountain, Lane County OR: earlier 30 ft tower 1933/34, 1947 lookout house on timber tower, lookout died at post 1952, removed or destroyed 1978-79; site gone.

facts.design: Earlier 30 ft 7x7 tower with ground cabin (1933 per register, 1934 per local history); 1947 14x14 lookout house on a timber tower (20 ft per register, 25 ft per local history)
facts.status_note: Tower removed or destroyed in 1978-79 (sources differ); no source describes what remains at the site now

staffing.status: staffed by a lookout and his wife in 1952; William Hastings died at his post

events.note: Register dates an earlier 30 ft 7x7 tower with a ground cabin to 1933
Local history dates a 30-foot round timber tower built by the Wendling CCC camp to 1934
14x14 lookout house on a timber tower; register says 20 ft, local history says 25 ft
William Hastings, 74, lookout for the Eastern Lane County Forest Protective association, died at his post on July 17; his wife shared the post
Firelookout.com says the tower was destroyed in 1978
Register says removed in 1979; local history says dismantled and salvaged in 1979
Registered March 30, 2011 as FFLOS US 914, OR 281

evidence.supports: earlier 30 ft 7x7 tower and ground cabin from 1933; 1947 20-foot treated timber tower; removed 1979
evidence.quote: Preceded by a 30' 7x7' tower and ground cabin living quarters from 1933, this 20' treated timber L-4 tower, built in 1947, was removed in 1979.

evidence.supports: William Hastings died at his post on July 17 after a heart attack

corrections.why: 9.1 m is 30 ft, the height of the earlier 1933/34 tower. The 1947 tower that stood until 1978-79 was 20 ft per the register (6.1 m) and 25 ft per the local history (7.6 m); the sources disagree and the editor should confirm before publishing.

resolved_conflicts.field: year of the earlier 30 ft tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register dates the 30 ft 7x7 tower and ground cabin to 1933; the local history dates a 30-foot round timber tower to 1934. Story reports both.
Register says 20 ft treated timber L-4 tower; local history says 25 ft. Story reports both.
Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1978; register and local history say removed, or dismantled and salvaged, in 1979. Story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 9.1 is the earlier 30 ft tower, not the 1947 tower; correction proposed with the disagreement stated. Staffing evidence is one 1952 item from The Forest Log, quoted by the local history. No source describes the site now and its access is not stated, so access is omitted. Firelookout.com repeats the 20 ft figure and gives 1978 as the year the tower was destroyed. No photo was added.
